### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx`  _(via RecordActivityProps (symbol, a top-level const object), showCommentInput (symbol, a field of const object RecordActivityProps, an authorable key of ui/RecordActivityProps), showCommentInput (literal, a string literal in refuseFeedTypesWithoutCommentBesideComposer))_
- `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`  _(via showCommentInput (symbol, a field of const object RecordActivityProps, an authorable key of ui/RecordActivityProps), showCommentInput (literal, a string literal in refuseFeedTypesWithoutCommentBesideComposer))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed45eb92880e5092889042df66c137399c2b5778` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c24c310563410435185c7a1ed8c07236fcb23d73` — the merge of head `906f6f6dcb3da83a94ab2090a2a6782f16ee833a` into base `ed45eb92880e5092889042df66c137399c2b5778`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c24c310563410435185c7a1ed8c07236fcb23d73 && git checkout c24c310563410435185c7a1ed8c07236fcb23d73
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ed45eb92880e5092889042df66c137399c2b5778 906f6f6dcb3da83a94ab2090a2a6782f16ee833a && git checkout -B drift-repro ed45eb92880e5092889042df66c137399c2b5778 && git merge --no-ff 906f6f6dcb3da83a94ab2090a2a6782f16ee833a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed45eb92880e5092889042df66c137399c2b5778
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ed45eb92880e5092889042df66c137399c2b5778` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:

- `RecordActivityProps` (the `record:activity` row of `ComponentPropsMap`): a present `types` array of strings without the exact entry `comment`, beside `showCommentInput` absent or `true`, moves from accepted to refused with one `custom` issue at `types`. RIGHT, and it is the card's Expected item 1 to the letter, message naming both fixes included.
- `RecordChatterProps.feed` (`record:chatter`, `record:discussion`): the same refusal at `feed.types`, because `feed` IS that object by reference. RIGHT, and wider than the card's wording, which names `record:activity` only. Judged against the renderer, not the PR body: `record-chatter.tsx` filters its rows with the same `applyFeedConfig` call on `feed.types`, hands `config.feed` to the timeline, and passes no `commentsShown`, so on that mount the composer is still drawn and a posted comment is filtered out of the feed it was posted to. The contradiction is real there and unguarded at render, so the refusal is owed on that mount more than on the first. Both prescribed fixes hold on it: an authored `feed` replaces the default feed whole, and the timeline reads `config.showCommentInput !== false`, so `feed.showCommentInput: false` does withdraw the composer.
- `types: []` beside the composer: refused. RIGHT. The renderer reads an empty list as a filter that keeps nothing, so it shows no comment either.
- `types: ['Comment', ...]` beside the composer: refused. RIGHT. `normalizeFeedTypes` and `feedTypesAdmitComments` match exactly; the spec check and the renderer judge agree on every string list.
- Unchanged, verified in the function: absent `types`; any `types` beside `showCommentInput: false`; a `types` that lists `comment`; a non-array or non-string-entry `types` (left to its own type issue); the open vocabulary (no entry is judged against the built-in kinds).
- A side effect named correctly by the PR: `types: ['commnet']` with the composer on is now refused, by this rule and not by name. The forced edit of the pre-existing case (fixture gains `showCommentInput: false`, assertion untouched) keeps that case reading the open vocabulary alone. RIGHT; the open-vocabulary ruling is not re-closed.

Public surface: no export added, removed or retyped. `.superRefine` on the closed object returns the same object class, so `.shape` readers (the lint unknown-key walker, the console mirror's `flatPropRefusals`) and the inferred type are unchanged; four other rows of the same file already carry an object-level refinement the same way. The published JSON Schema does not carry the rule: the ledger gains exactly the two sites the diff names (`ui/RecordActivityProps` root, `ui/RecordChatterProps` `feed`), with the measured counts moved by two and two. RIGHT as a ledger entry; the gate that holds the ledger to the build is in Build Core, still pending (below).

Doors reached, read in the cited code: `validateComponentProps` parses `properties` against the row and emits every non-key verdict at `error` as `component-props-invalid` at `properties.` plus the issue path, so `properties.types` and `properties.feed.types` are the paths the entry and changeset state; the rule is registered for every CLI command and on the runtime page save door. The boot, hydration and read paths run no authoring rule, so a stored page carrying the shape still loads and renders (composer withheld on `record:activity`), and its next save is refused. The semantic entry's `surface` says exactly this. One door the changeset does not name: the console mirror takes the row by reference through `stripImportedDefaults`, checks included, so `safeValidateSchema` and `objectui validate` refuse the shape the same day (N2).

Gate verdicts on this head, as the check-runs read when this record was written. Success: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint and Repo Gates, Lint ESLint, Lint docs and code guards, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint CI release and engine gates, Lint PM dispatch-gates, both scoped lint jobs with the tooling self-tests, Type Check source gates, Type Check debt ledger, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check PR Size, and the aggregate Dogfood Regression Gate. PENDING, not verdicts: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Build Core, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Type Check UI, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates. This PASS is the contract judgment; it does not stand in for any pending check, and landing waits on them.

### ② Semver level

`Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the right kind (a value combination refused), and the kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves: the changeset is `@objectstack/spec: minor`. RIGHT. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is on the PR body and the changeset body, line-initial, and is the correct arm: nothing widens. The BREAKING banner is present, the FROM to TO lines and the one-line fix are in the body, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker registers the D3 entry by its id; the entry file exists under the step-18 semantic entries with that id. No conversion is the right disposition: which of the two fixes the author meant cannot be derived from the stored value, and the two render differently. Check Changeset concluded success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: contract review owed at this head. Answered by this record.
- Deviation, forced test change: accepted, judged in ① above.
- Deviation, `check:test-typecheck` needed a larger heap locally: environmental; CI's Type Check debt ledger concluded success, Type Check workspace and consumer gates are pending.
- Deviation, HTTP page door not driven end to end: accepted on the reading of the rule's registration (every command, runtime `page` door) and of the rule body, which treats this issue as any other value verdict. No special path exists for it to miss.
- Dogfood battery: NOT MEASURED by the dev at hand-off, and the card's unblock and claim comments both say this narrowing owes it. On this head the dogfood shard matrix job and Dogfood Verify CLI read skipped, and the aggregate Dogfood Regression Gate reads success. A skipped shard is not a run of the battery. ESCALATED to the lane seat: the battery reading the card owes is a landing condition this record does not supply.
- Out-of-scope finding, the chatter mount still draws the composer for a host composing `RecordChatterPanel` in code: confirmed in the renderer (no `commentsShown` handed to the timeline). Authored pages can no longer reach it after this change. ESCALATED to the seat for a ui-lane card; not a defect of this diff.
- Out-of-scope carrier, HotCRM `lead_detail`: carried separately per the card. The in-repo copy of that page is the published 4.0.1 fixture, which is replayed through boot hydration and the registry, never through the props gate, so it stays as published.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no read, no id materialisation and no join.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`, against the ruling it implements (the spec-lane half of #34371 option A, as card #34383 states it) and its first consumers. The check holds sentence by sentence against the code it cites: both renderers filter by the allow-list; the `record:activity` renderer withholds the composer through `feedTypesAdmitComments`, which is on main; the parsed value carries the default `true` while the console mirror strips defaults, and `!== false` is the one reading true at both doors; absent `types` returns before any judgment; matching is exact as the renderers match; a list with a non-string entry is left to its element issue. The two `.describe()` texts state the rule and neither contradicts the open-vocabulary jsdoc above `types`. Attempts to break it: a null or scalar `types` (returns, type issue stands alone); a mixed list (returns); an unknown key beside it (strict refusal kept, pinned); the nested mount (path is `feed.types`, pinned on both block names); a stored page at boot (not judged); the mirror with defaults stripped (same verdict). None broke it.

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.record-activity-types-without-comment-beside-composer-refused.ts`, against ADR-0087 D3 and the doors it names. `surface`, `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` each agree with the code: the doors, the two finding paths, the rule id, the measured producer shape (present verbatim in the published HotCRM fixture), and the absence of a mechanical rewrite. It names both mounts, so an operator reading the upgrade guide is not told the rule is `record:activity` only.

`packages/spec/src/ui/component.test.ts` and the ledger, as the narrowing floor: the nine cases pin the refused shape, both fixed shapes and an absent `types`, which is the card's Expected item 3, plus both mounts through `ComponentPropsMap`. The ledger rows match the two refinement sites and nothing else.

The narrowing itself, against the published spec on main: it does not take a declared capability away at the consumer. The spec on main declares `types` as the kinds the feed shows and `showCommentInput` as a composer on that feed; no sentence of it promises a composer whose posts the same feed hides, the `record:activity` renderer already refuses to draw one, and the maintainer's ruling chose refusal at authoring over a derived default. Both remaining capabilities stay reachable in one key each (a comment-taking feed, a comment-free feed). This makes the spec's own reading real where it is written.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits, none of which moves the head:

- N1 (nit) — `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx`, hand-written and outside the diff, now states the opposite of the rule in one sentence (authoring `types: ['approval']` "is legal, typechecks, builds") and is incomplete in two table cells (`types: []` renders an empty timeline; `showCommentInput` needs only a host context). The docs-drift check named this page on this PR. So `Skills-docs: none` is not the whole truth: on the PR body, a prose face, the line should read follow-up owed naming that file, with a docs card filed.
- N2 (nit) — the changeset's "What moves" names the CLI and page doors but not the console mirror (`@object-ui/types/zod`, `safeValidateSchema`, `objectui validate`), which refuses the shape by reference from the same release. Accepted deviation, or a line in the follow-up docs card.
- N3 (nit) — no detector in `refused-shapes.ts`, so the stored-metadata preview does not list an installed page carrying the shape before its next save is refused. Most refused entries of step 18 have none, so this is no rule broken; a follow-up card if the seat wants the HotCRM case named to operators ahead of the save.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept set between the heads: UNCHANGED, read off the function and not off the account. The body of `refuseFeedTypesWithoutCommentBesideComposer` differs between the heads in one token, the `path` of the one `addIssue` call (`['types']` to `['showCommentInput']`), plus docblock prose. The three guards are byte-identical: return unless `types` is an array and `showCommentInput` is not `false`; return unless every entry is a string; return when the list includes the exact entry `comment`. The message text is identical. The attachment is identical: one `.superRefine` on `RecordActivityProps`, and `RecordChatterProps.feed` is still that object by reference, so both sites carry the same condition. Is `showCommentInput` the right address. YES, on three readings of the tree:
- The rule's own subject. `types` alone is a valid value on any list of strings (the open-vocabulary ruling, restated in the jsdoc directly above the key); what the feed cannot honour is the composer beside it. The composer key is the one whose value, written or defaulted, asks for the thing the list rules out, and it is the key the second prescribed fix edits. The first fix edits `types`; the message opens by naming `types` and the authored list verbatim and still names both ways out (`add 'comment' to types`, `set showCommentInput: false`), both pinned by text.
- An address the author did not write. On the measured producer shape the key is absent and the default is what is refused, so the finding points at a key not in the document. That is the normal shape of a path for a defaulted or missing key (a missing required key is addressed the same way), the lint finding path is a string and nothing resolves it against the source, and the message says `showCommentInput (default true)`. Accepted.
- Precedent in the same file: the other cross-key refinements address the key that carries the contradicted request (`count`, `label`, `target`, `onSuccess`, `params`), not the container beside it.

Root cause or a dodge of the UI test. Root cause. `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` on the live tree (`specMemberVerdict`) probes one key at a time: for `record:activity.types`, declared `array` of `string` in the registry, it parses `{ types: ['...'] }` alone, keeps only issues whose first path segment is `types`, and reads any issue AT the container node (path length one) as `no-member-position`, meaning the contract refused the container. On the old head the single-key probe met the sibling's default `true`, the cross-key issue sat at `types`, and the probe read a string member of an accepted list as a container refusal. The test's reading is sound for what it measures (it is how a named-shape object or a wrong container kind speaks), and it was not edited: the PR touches no `ui/**` file. The spec issue was what misstated the fact: it said `types` where the contract has no complaint about `types`. At the new head the probe sees a complaint about a sibling only, which that test defines as `accepts`, and that is the true answer to its question (a string member IS admitted). The same holds for the arm probe (`specArmVerdict`), the `showCommentInput` probe (`{ showCommentInput: true }` alone carries no `types`, so the rule does not fire), and the `feed` probes on the chatter rows (an empty or probe-keyed `feed` never reaches the rule). No single-key judge now reads the rule at all, which is correct for a rule about a pair.

Other readers of the address, searched on the live tree: `validate-component-props.ts` (generic, no path special-cased); `authoring-rules.ts` (registration only); `refused-shapes.ts` (no detector for this shape, as before); the console mirror (takes the row by reference, so the issue path moves with it and nothing there names it); no test or snapshot under `ui/**` or `packages/**` names `properties.types`, `feed.types` or the card number outside the PR's own pin.
